sentences.text: Researchers employed a retrospective design to analyze dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI brain scans from 59 subjects collected on a 3.0 T scanner.
The image data was divided into 4,956 pairs for training, 1,180 for validation, and 59 for testing.

The new method was compared against four other registration techniques, including ANTs, a CNN-based model, GWMS, and C2FViT, and it required the least time to train while maintaining a competitive speed for processing each case.
This approach generated the smoothest time-intensity curves in the artery, venous, and white matter regions, exhibiting the lowest error values among the tested methods.
The authors conclude that the new method offers accuracy similar to the best existing methods while being significantly more computationally efficient.
